title: The challenge of defending against bulletproof dead drops on public blockchains
description: Threat actors are increasingly using public blockchain networks to host malware command-and-control (C2) configurations, leveraging the immutable and decentralized nature of blockchains to create resilient, bulletproof dead drops. This approach eliminates single points of failure common in traditional C2 infrastructures, making takedown efforts by defenders ineffective. By embedding encrypted C2 data in blockchain transactions and retrieving it via read-only RPC queries, adversaries bypass domain seizures and perimeter defenses. This evolution challenges traditional defensive models reliant on domain blocklists and infrastructure takedowns, requiring new detection strategies focused on anomalous blockchain-related traffic and endpoint memory analysis.
